156.stem: Match the device to its symbol characteristic:
156.why: Diode – Arrowhead; Transistor – Three terminals; Resistor – Zig-zag line.

64.why: A resistor limits current, a capacitor stores energy, a diode passes current one way and a transistor amplifies.

65.why: Capacitors filter and store energy, transistors switch and amplify, rectifiers convert AC to DC and Zener diodes regulate voltage.

73.why: Wi-Fi is a wireless LAN, optical fibre carries data as light, Bluetooth is short-range wireless and cellular networks serve mobile phones.

78.why: A modem connects to the Internet, a switch connects devices in a LAN, a router routes data between networks and a repeater extends signal range.
R: Connects multiple devices in a LAN

80.why: Wireless media need no cables, wired media use cables such as Ethernet, optical fibre uses light and radio waves are used for broadcasting.
R: Uses light for high-speed data transfer
Used for broadcasting and wireless communication

86.why: A table stores data in rows and columns, a primary key identifies a record, SQL queries databases and a record is a single row.
R: Stores data in rows and columns
A single row in a table

87.why: Relational databases use tables, NoSQL databases handle large unstructured data, distributed databases spread across locations and object-oriented databases store objects.
R: Handles large volumes of unstructured data

90.why: An index speeds retrieval, a view is a virtual table from a query, a trigger runs on certain events and a schema defines the structure.

94.why:
inserts an image,
    an unordered list and tabular data.

114.why: A transistor amplifies, an LED emits light, a diode rectifies and a Zener diode regulates voltage.

115.why: OR is logical sum, NOT inversion, NAND an inverted product and AND a logical product.

116.why: N-type has electrons as majority carriers, P-type holes; extrinsic semiconductors are doped and intrinsic ones have equal electrons and holes.

117.why: In a BJT the base controls current, the emitter supplies carriers and the collector collects them; in a FET the gate is the control terminal.

154.why: The base is very thin, the collector is the largest and the emitter is heavily doped.

155.why: A reverse-biased diode has very high resistance; a forward-biased diode has low resistance.

157.why: A half-wave rectifier uses one diode, a centre-tap full-wave rectifier two and a bridge rectifier four.

158.why: Extrinsic semiconductors are doped; intrinsic ones are pure.

224.why: A bus uses a single cable, a ring a circular path, a star a central hub and a mesh interconnects every node.

225.why: FTP transfers files, HTTP serves web pages, TCP gives reliable delivery and SMTP sends email.

226.why: A router routes packets, a repeater boosts signals, a gateway converts between protocols and a bridge connects LANs.

227.why: A telephone is full duplex, radio broadcasting simplex, a walkie-talkie half duplex, and multiplexing sends many signals over one link.

228.why: NFC works over a few centimetres, Bluetooth over a few metres, Wi-Fi over tens of metres and cellular networks over kilometres.

229.why: Optical fibre is glass or plastic, radio waves are electromagnetic, twisted pair uses copper wires and coaxial cable is shielded copper.

249.why: INSERT is DML, COMMIT TCL, CREATE DDL and GRANT DCL.

250.why: A relation is a table, a tuple a row, a domain the set of permitted values and an attribute a column.

252.why: DROP TABLE removes a table, DELETE removes rows, CREATE TABLE makes a new table and ALTER TABLE changes its structure.
